# wlcs tests expected to fail in the phase tier, one gtest name per line (`Suite.test` or
# `Suite/Param.test/N`), each followed by `# <id>`; the ids are the rows below.
# dev/wlcs/run.sh --phase excludes them with --gtest_filter=-... (A6): never run and ignored,
# because each wlcs timeout costs 10 s. Regenerated by lane P0-wlcs against casement itself
# (wlcs-casement drives casement-testkit's Fixture: the real State on the headless backend; the
# earlier list was for a smithay stand-in). The whole suite (1225 tests run, 1291 gtest lines listed),
# one jailed run of about 80 s, after P0-smithay: 871 pass, 23 fail (listed here), 331 skip (wl_shell
# and zxdg_shell_v6 are not served, wlcs' own xfail self-tests). Before it (P0-popups): 857 pass,
# 37 fail; before that (P0-layer-geom): 829 pass, 65 fail; before that: 596 pass, 298 fail. The list
# may only shrink. Lane wlcs of wave 2026-10-15 removed six rows (17 left): the two text-input
# ordering tests, the three decoration configure tests and the W9 touch test; unrun until the
# orchestrator's wlcs run confirms them. Lane fork of wave 2 (smithay fork patches, written without a
# build or a run) removed eight more (9 left): the three xdg_wm_base `get_xdg_surface` error tests (W3),
# `wm_capabilities_are_sent` (W4) and the four subsurface position tests (W7).
# `CopyCutPaste.given_source_has_offered_when_sink_gets_focus_it_sees_offer` failed now and then in a
# 12-way shard run: the shim activated a mapped window a pass after the commit that mapped it, and a
# client that set the selection right after its roundtrip could be ahead of that (11 failures in 300
# runs under 12-way load; none in 300 after). A window that maps is now activated in the commit that
# maps it (casement::relax, `testing` only); it is not listed.
#
# Shim policies that decide what counts as a failure (wlcs-casement/src/host.rs):
#   - A37 (casement::relax, `testing` only): a buffer attached before the first ack is taken as the
#     ack and maps the window, as the compositors wlcs was written for do.
#   - a window that maps is activated with a valid token, in the commit that maps it, because wlcs
#     takes a newly mapped window to be the active one and casement keys no window nobody asked for
#     (A7).
#   - a window dropped by an interactive move glides to rest (the shim advances the clock by a second
#     at each button release), and a toplevel that maps again after a null buffer is put back where
#     wlcs had put it by hand.
#   - touch coordinates are whole pixels: wlcs' header says wl_fixed_t but its helpers (pinned SHA
#     and upstream main) pass plain ints.
#   - `position_window_absolute` on a layer surface pins it (`Event::LayerPlaced`): its anchors would
#     not let wlcs' layer-layer tests put two surfaces side by side.
#
# W1 (layer-shell) and W2 (xdg window geometry) were fixed by P0-layer-geom, W5 (wl_surface.enter and
#     leave) by P0-output-enter, W6 by P0-dead-focus; they have no entries left. W8, W10 and W13 were
#     fixed by P0-popups (FINDINGS.md "P0-popups"). The ids stay unused so the other rows keep names.
# W3: the three get_xdg_surface error tests (role, attached buffer, committed buffer) are FIXED in the
#     smithay fork (wm_base.rs, GetXdgSurface: `role` and `invalid_surface_state` on the xdg_wm_base).
#     Kept:
#       - attaching_buffer_to_unconfigured_xdg_surface_is_an_error: the test attaches the buffer and
#         roundtrips with no commit, and expects `unconfigured_buffer` on the attach. The XML says
#         the error is for a surface that "has a buffer attached before the first configure" and
#         smithay checks it where a buffer takes effect, in the commit (wl_surface.attach itself
#         is smithay's compositor module and knows nothing of xdg). It is also the very rule the
#         A37 relaxation switches off for wlcs. Casement and the fork both raise it at the commit.
#     The zero-size anchor (set_anchor_rect), the fractional-scale and viewporter error objects, the
#     viewporter bad_size hook and out_of_buffer are FIXED in the fork (P0-smithay, branch
#     casement-textinput; FINDINGS.md "P0-smithay").
# W4: wlcs-side expectations that contradict the protocol XML; not a casement bug.
#       - xdg_toplevel.wm_capabilities_are_sent: FIXED in the fork (the event goes out at get_toplevel,
#         version 5 and up, capabilities only; no configure, which would break the text-input order).
#       - XdgDecorationV1Test.set_mode_client/server and unset_mode "results in a configure event"
#         were W4 too: the toplevel never commits, so no xdg_surface.configure is due yet. FIXED in
#         the shim's policy (casement::relax, `testing` only): under the lenient policy the initial
#         configure goes out with the decoration's answer, as the decoration XML allows ("a
#         configure event can be sent at any time"). Not listed.
#       - XdgDecorationV1Test.destroying_toplevel_before_decoration_throws_orphaned: wlcs expects the
#         error on zxdg_decoration_manager_v1; xdg-decoration-unstable-v1.xml defines `orphaned` in
#         zxdg_toplevel_decoration_v1's own enum, and smithay raises it there. Kept: moving it to the
#         manager would break the XML to satisfy the test.
# W7: subsurface tests on an xdg parent. Diagnosed 2026-10-15 from subsurfaces.cpp and smithay's
#     wayland/compositor. FIXED in the fork (compositor/placement.rs, tree.rs): wl_subsurface.set_position
#     is state of the PARENT (cached with the parent's commit, applied with the parent's state, so a
#     grandchild needs its parent's and then its grandparent's commit), and a sync child of a non-sync
#     parent takes only what the child committed, not its pending state. The four position tests are no
#     longer listed. Kept: place_below_simple and place_above_simple both assert the focused surface is
#     neither of the two subsurfaces that cover the pointer (Ne(a), Ne(b)), which no compositor that
#     gives a subsurface the pointer can satisfy; wlcs-side.
# W8: FIXED by P0-popups: popup grabs (a release, a press, a key or a touch is the proof, if it is the
#     client's latest input), the grab of a nested popup with its parent's serial, popup_done when
#     another toplevel is activated, the pointer's leave when a popup is destroyed under it, reactive
#     popups, a reposition taking effect at the ack. The one entry left (zero-size anchor) is W3.
# W9: FIXED 2026-10-15 (lane wlcs). wlcs puts the parent at y = -5 for touch_on_surface_seen/
#     subsurface_at_x7_y12; casement keeps a floating window inside the usable area, which is the
#     person-facing rule (a drag never hides a title bar under the bar) and stays. A position a test
#     asks for is a different thing: the shim's placement is Event::WindowPlaced, which layout
#     takes as given (WindowPlacement::Placed, size still fitted) until the person drags the window
#     or it unmaps. Not listed.
# W10: FIXED by P0-popups: a move or resize takes the pointer from the window (xdg_toplevel.move:
#     "the surface will lose the focus of the device") and gives it back at the release; the shim lets
#     a dropped window glide to rest.
# W12: smithay policy that wlcs, written against Mir, does not meet; fixable only in the smithay fork or
#     by re-implementing the piece in casement. Not a casement bug in the sense of the protocol.
#       - PrimarySelection (4) and CopyCutPaste.given_sink_has_focus_...: a source that has no keyboard
#         focus sets the selection (with serial 0); smithay ignores set_selection from a client that
#         does not have the keyboard focus (data_device/device.rs and primary_selection/device.rs).
#         The protocols allow either; the sink never sees an offer.
#       - A kept decision, not a gap: a program the person is not using (no keyboard focus) cannot
#         replace the selection or the clipboard. The row stays until smithay offers a policy hook.
#       - TextInputV3WithInputMethodV2Test: nine of eleven FIXED in the fork by P0-smithay (enter with
#         keyboard focus whether or not an input method exists; an input method that binds after the
#         field was enabled is activated for it); the last two are W14.
# W14: wlcs run 2026-10-15 (910 pass, 5 fail) showed the 2026-10-15 shim fix (xdg_shell::
#     map_keyed_on_first_buffer: enter before the first configure) was right but not enough, and
#     that text_input_enters_grabbing_popup and text_input_enters_parent_surface_after_child_destroyed
#     cannot pass on a compositor that follows xdg-shell. Both open with `InSequence`, so every
#     EXPECT_CALL the xdg helpers make afterwards (XdgSurfaceStable::configure at src/xdg_shell_
#     stable.cpp:27, then XdgToplevelStable configure/close/configure_bounds/wm_capabilities at
#     83-86, then the popup's) joins one chain, and gmock RETIRES every earlier link of the chain
#     as soon as a later one is called (RetireAllPreRequisites). The wire order of a configure is
#     fixed by the protocol: xdg_toplevel.configure_bounds / configure, THEN xdg_surface.configure,
#     and for a popup xdg_popup.configure THEN xdg_surface.configure; the chain wants the opposite,
#     so the second event of every pair is "Unexpected ... it is retired" (the log shows exactly
#     that for the parent's configure(0,0) and configure(1492), and for the popup's configure
#     (1498)). Besides, wm_capabilities goes out at get_toplevel (the fork, for
#     wm_capabilities_are_sent), before the commit that gives the keyboard enter, so it also
#     precedes `enter(parent)`. The text-input `enter` itself does arrive in the right place. Only
#     a compositor that sends the parent and the popup no configure at all in that window passes;
#     that would break the protocol (and every wlcs test that reads the first configure). Kept.
# W13: FIXED in the shim (casement was right: a toplevel unmapped by a null buffer is configured again
#     and maps again with fresh state; xdg_toplevel's "Unmapping" says it returns to its initial state).
#     wlcs puts the surface back where it was and re-attaches at once; the shim now remembers where
#     wlcs put each toplevel and puts a window that maps again there. Test:
#     casement-testkit/tests/relax.rs (passes with and without the shim: casement needed no change).
